title: phoenix: floats always encoded as f64, not shortest form
description: phnx-im/mimi-content main 31487f9 and PR #20 head 6378938 encode every cbor::Value::Float as a double (src/cbor.rs Value::encode: e.f64; PR #20 comment: 'Encoding always uses f64, so the bytes a message hashes to do not depend on which widths the encoder could shorten'). draft-ietf-mimi-content-08/-09 §6.1 L1870-1876 and -10 §6.1 L1927-1933: documents MUST use RFC 8949 §4.2.1 deterministic serialization, 'using the shortest CBOR encoding of integers, tags, and floats' (1.5 is f9 3e00, not fb 3ff8000000000000). Evidence: crates/mimi-content/tests/fixtures/phoenix/float.cbor (extension x-float = 1.5); mimid refuses it with DecodeError::NotShortestForm (tests/phoenix_fixtures.rs float_extension_value). -10 §6.1 also says receivers are not expected to strictly enforce encoding size, so this is also evidence for mimid decision bead mimid-1wgh.2.27. Report upstream only with Mark's OK.
